articles.author: Caitlin Flanagan
articles.summary: I have Wi-Fi. I have a human heart. Of course I fired up the 60-second spot for Novig, a sports betting company. I was drawn not by the pulchritude of Sydney Sweeney, although that is undeniable, but by the many accounts of female athletes being enraged by the ad. I myself can’t catch a wiffle ball on an airless day, but I was born before Title IX, in the time when girls were allowed to follow their interests and make something of themselves. Still, I wanted to see what the commotion was about. By the end of the ad, I wondered if I’d found the wrong one because the ad I saw didn’t concern women athletes in any remote way. It’s a sleek ad featuring the world’s sexiest woman saying the word sports over and over again, and if that isn’t an inducement to the average online sports bettor (overwhelmingly young and male), nothing is. I knew that the ad was stirring up something powerful because of the moralizing terms with which the press described Sweeney’s appearance in the ad. stories.summary: Kenya will host the World Athletics Championships in 2029, in a first for the African continent. Nairobi beat London and Rome for the honor, after what the World Athletics president called a “ compelling and emotional bid .” Kenya is the second-most successful nation in the history of the World Championships, and yet it has never hosted the event. Nairobi narrowly lost out on hosting in 2025 due to infrastructure concerns, but has since conducted significant renovations on the Kasarani Stadium, which will host the athletes. The announcement comes as part of a slew of sporting wins for Kenya and the continent: Nairobi is co-hosting next year’s Africa Cup of Nations alongside Tanzania and Uganda, while the Youth Olympic Games — the first Olympic event to ever be held in Africa — is due to kick off in Dakar, Senegal, next month. — Paige Bruton
